thread:
Omar: Quick question  We're finalizing Dedicated "burst handoff" behavior when reserved pool hits soft limit. Two choices: immediate spillover to fallback models (best-effort), or graceful degradation with queued throttles + notify. Need a GA default.

Keiko: Immediate spillover avoids errors but can change model outputs. Not great for customers who need strict determinism.

Lena: Graceful degradation (queue/throttle) keeps output consistent but increases latency. For GA, prefer conservative: notify + gradual throttling, then spillover as last resort.

Marco: Ops note: if we throttle, we must prevent head-of-line blocking. Use request prioritization and token bucket per-tenant. Also alert on throttle spikes.

Omar: Product proposal: default = graceful degrade with 2-tier action: 1) soft-throttle at 10% over reserved for up to 5m, 2) if sustained, route to compat-fallback model for non-critical routes. Block critical routes from automatic spillover unless customer opts in.

Keiko: Add config: per-route opt-in for spillover + console flag for "preserve-output". Also telemetry: "route-fallback-count" and "throttle-events".

Lena: Runbook: pager only if >3 tenants throttled concurrently for >30m. Otherwise just alert and auto-remediate.

Marco: Implementation: router will evaluate route metadata; if route.meta.allow_spill=true then spillover immediate, else apply throttles. Need unit tests covering canary + spillover during reclaimed cushion.

ops-bot: scheduled: create-epic "burst-handoff-defaults" assigned to @Omar,@Keiko,@Lena,@Marco due 2025-06-01

Omar: Locking: default = graceful degradation -> throttles -> selective spillover opt-in. We'll document as GA behavior and add migration notes for customers who want immediate spillover.

Keiko: I'll add the console toggle and per-route docs.

Lena: I'll update runbook and alerts.

Marco: I'll add router checks and tests.

Omar: Thanks all. If nobody objects by EOD Monday we'll ship this as default. :thumbsup:
